Viable

VY-uh-bul — starts like 'via'; a viable plan has a real way to work (and comes from a root meaning 'able to live'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Viable is capable of actually working and succeeding in practice.

Solar panels have become a viable option for many ordinary homeowners.

Worked Example

Two students pitch fundraisers to the club. One plan requires renting a stadium the school could never afford. The other is a bake sale using the cafeteria they already have — it could start this weekend.

The bake sale can actually succeed with real resources, so it is viable. Unlike 'ideal,' which describes the perfect option, viable describes one that can genuinely work.

How Viable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

feasible

feasible: possible to accomplish

workable

workable: able to function in practice

practical

practical: realistic and sensible to carry out

Antonyms

impossible

impossible: not able to be done at all

impractical

impractical: not realistic to carry out

How Strong Is It? — conceivable → viable → foolproof

conceivable vs. viable

conceivable vs. viable: Conceivable is weaker than viable — a conceivable plan can merely be imagined, while a viable one can actually be carried out successfully.

foolproof vs. viable

foolproof vs. viable: Foolproof is stronger than viable: a viable plan can work, but a foolproof plan is guaranteed to work no matter what goes wrong.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — vi-

root — vi-: life (Latin (vita, via French vie))

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: capable of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: French vie (life, from Latin vita) plus -able gives 'able to live.' A viable seed can survive and grow — and by extension, a viable plan can survive contact with reality.

Use the root in a new word: vital

Use the root in a new word: vital: Clean water is vital to the health of every community.

Word Choice

Viable is used to judge plans, businesses, and options on whether they can really work; in biology it describes organisms or seeds able to survive.
